item.title: Work-life balance: the Ticino survey starts
item.description: Pro Familia Svizzera Italiana launches the first cantonal survey to map flexibility, working hours and leave in Ticino companies.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - First cantonal survey on work-life balance - Promoted by Pro Familia Svizzera Italiana - Official start of the survey: 1 October - Objective: to map good practices and areas for improvement
## Key Facts - Promoter: Pro Familia Svizzera Italiana - Start date: 1 October - Target: Employers in the canton - Data analysis: Dr. Philippe Gnaegi
The first cantonal survey dedicated to the issue of work-life balance, an initiative promoted by Pro Familia Svizzera Italiana that aims to involve all employers active in the Ticino area, officially started on 1 October. The primary objective of this survey is to bring out the good practices already implemented within companies and local authorities, while identifying the areas where action is needed to make concrete improvements. The survey, which aims to offer a representative snapshot of the Ticino economic reality, focuses on crucial aspects of personnel management, such as work flexibility, hours, different organizational models, leave policies, career opportunities and gender balance. ### A data-driven approach. The process of analyzing the data collected will be managed by Dr. Philippe Gnaegi, a university professor who has over twenty years of specific experience in the sector. The results will be processed exclusively in aggregate form, ensuring the anonymity of the individual participating realities. The initiative is not limited to the simple collection of data, but intends to provide institutions, the political world and the economic fabric with a solid and concrete basis on which to build future measures to support businesses. In a historical moment characterized by a widespread shortage of qualified personnel, the ability of a company to reconcile professional and personal needs becomes a determining factor for its attractiveness on the labor market. ### Impact on the competitiveness of the territory. The reconciliation of work and private life is not only a matter of individual well-being, but a fundamental pillar for the competitiveness of the Ticino territory as a whole. According to the promoters, companies that adopt flexible models that are attentive to the needs of employees are in a position of competitive advantage, being able to attract and retain the talents necessary for business growth more easily. The survey aims precisely to crystallize this added value, making visible the strategies that make organizations more resilient and attractive. For employers in the Canton, participating in this survey means actively contributing to the definition of a regulatory and support framework that is more in line with the real needs of the market. The comparison with industry practices also allows them to assess their positioning compared to the competition. Find out more about personnel management to understand how company policies influence the local labor market. The collection of structured data will allow, in perspective, to develop targeted interventions that can support Ticino companies in overcoming the challenges related to the management of schedules and the enhancement of employees. This evidence-based approach is essential to avoid fragmented interventions, preferring instead support policies that take into account the specificity of the cantonal economic fabric. The analysis conducted by Dr. Philippe Gnaegi ensures the scientific rigor that is essential to translate the responses of companies into operational guidelines, capable of positively influencing the attractiveness of the Ticino economic system for the years to come.
## Recommended tools For an updated estimate, use the net salary calculator and the CHF-EUR exchange comparator. ### How to contribute to the improvement of the system. The active participation of employers is the main driver of this survey. By sharing their organizational models, companies can make an essential contribution to guiding future institutional strategies. The anonymous and aggregate nature of the analysis, as specified by Pro Familia Svizzera Italiana, ensures that the confidentiality of company information is preserved, while allowing a reliable overview to be obtained. Companies wishing to learn more about issues related to personnel management and the impact of wage costs can consult the dedicated online services. For proper corporate financial planning, it is useful to regularly monitor changes in social security contributions and current regulations. If your company is looking to optimize its wage structure or wants to assess the impact of personnel costs, our calcolatore stipendio is a useful tool for obtaining accurate and up-to-date estimates. The Pro Familia initiative represents a unique opportunity for Ticino companies to make their voices heard in the debate on job quality. The success of the survey will depend on the capillarity of participation, which will allow to outline a shared strategy between the public and private sectors. We invite employers to consider the importance of this survey for the construction of a more solid, flexible labor market capable of responding to contemporary challenges, while ensuring greater stability for all organizations operating in the Canton.

item.title: Novartis and Abogen: RNA license for up to 7.2 billion
item.description: Novartis obtains the worldwide license on ABO2203 from Abogen: 575 million initial dollars and potential payments up to about 7.2 billion.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Novartis obtains worldwide license on ABO2203. - Abogen receives an initial $575 million. - The agreement can reach about 7.2 billion. - ABO2203 mRNA is used against B lymphocytes.
## Key Facts - Active ingredient: ABO2203 - License: Worldwide Exclusive - Initial payment: $575 million - Value: CHF 480 million - Potential: up to approximately $7.2 billion - Technology: mRNA - Development: clinical phase
### The structure of the agreement Novartis expands its portfolio of RNA-based therapeutics thanks to a license agreement with Abogen Biosciences, a Chinese biotech company. The agreement was communicated by Abogen itself in a note.
At the heart is ABO2203, a new active ingredient for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. The agreement gives Novartis an exclusive worldwide license on the active ingredient and provides options on additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
The expected initial payment for Abogen is $575 million, or CHF 480 million. The potential portion of the transaction can be as high as $7.2 billion if all options on the other programs are exercised and the respective development, approval and commercialization milestones are met.
Abogen will also be entitled to possible licensing revenue on future sales of the products. The structure therefore combines an initial component, a part related to milestones and a possible return on sales.
### How does ABO2203 ABO2203 uses mRNA, the messenger ribonucleic acid, to induce the body to produce a molecule on its own that attacks and eliminates B lymphocytes in a targeted manner. These cells play an important role in many autoimmune diseases. According to Abogen, the drug is already in clinical development.
RNA technology had made a lot of headlines especially thanks to the Covid vaccines from Moderna and Biontech. However, it has existed for several decades and had previously been tested mainly in cancer research. The press release thus puts in the same agreement an active ingredient already in clinical development and a platform from which other programs can derive. ## What does potential value mean
To read the agreement from an economic point of view, it is necessary to keep separate the initial payment, the conditions for subsequent payments and the possible revenues related to sales. The figure of about 7.2 billion is not presented as an initial outlay: the source links it to the exercise of all options and the achievement of the expected goals.
### The components of the agreement
| Voice | Practical reading | |---|---| | Initial payment | USD 575 million, with an indicated value of CHF 480 million. | | Options | Additional programs based on Abogen's RNA platform. | | Milestones | Development, approval and commercialisation of the programmes concerned. | | Future Sales | Possible licensing revenue for Abogen. |
The correct comparison is therefore not between two sums available at the same time. The $575 million is reported as the initial payment; instead, the maximum value depends on a sequence of conditions. All options for the other programs must be exercised first, then the respective development, approval, and commercialization milestones must be met.
For a reader in Switzerland, the reference to 480 million francs makes the scale of the initial component immediate, while the total potential remains expressed in dollars. The currency, however, does not change the structure of the agreement: the first amount and the maximum potential belong to different times and conditions.
The scientific profile must also be read separately from the commercial one. ABO2203 is described as already in clinical development, but the agreement also links additional payments to approval and marketing. The text therefore distinguishes the development of the drug from the steps necessary to get to sales.
For the daily life of residents, the concrete connection remains informative: the source describes a transaction between companies, not a payment intended for families. To distinguish the company figure from one's income, you can use the calcolatore stipendio; those who want to follow the labor market can consult the aziende che assumono.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## A control board for the reader
### Five operational steps
1. **Identify the object.** The first reference is ABO2203, an active ingredient intended for the treatment of autoimmune diseases. This avoids confusing it with the broader RNA-based platform.
2. Separate license and options. The license granted to Novartis is exclusive and worldwide for ABO2203. The options instead cover additional drug programs based on Abogen's RNA platform.
3. Record the amount and currency. The initial payment should be recorded as 575 million dollars, with the indicated equivalent of 480 million francs. The two figures describe the same initial payment, not two separate payments.
4. Rebuild the condition for the maximum. The value of up to about $7.2 billion requires the exercise of all options and the achievement of development, approval and commercialization goals. The figure should therefore be read as a scenario subject to these steps.
5. Keep future sales separate. Abogen may have possible license revenue on future product sales. This item should not be confused with either the initial payment or the milestones listed above.
The reading procedure allows you to update the news without adding external estimates. Each new element should be traced back to one of five steps: the active ingredient, options, initial amount, milestones or future sales.
On a scientific level, two pieces of information from the source remain central: ABO2203 mRNA is used to target B lymphocytes and the drug is already in clinical development. On the economic level, however, the decisive fact is the distinction between the initial payment and payments subject to subsequent phases.

item.title: Average salary by profession Switzerland 2026: St. Gallen
item.description: 2026 comparison between professions, cantons and sectors: AHV contributions, BVG, taxes on three levels and KVG to read the canton of St. Gallen.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - No federal minimum wage; some cantons have one - AHV/IV/EO: 5.3% to be paid by the employee - KVG mandatory for residents within 3 months of arrival - Taxation is federal, cantonal and municipal
## Key Facts - Focus → canton of St. Gallen and national comparison - FSO/BFS → statistics - AHV/IV/EO → 5.3% employee, 10.6% total with employer - AD/AC → 1.1% up to the annual ceiling - UVG/LAA → 0.7–1.5% depending on the sector - Maximum hours → 45 or 50 hours per week - Minimum holidays → 4 weeks, 5 under 20 years old - Maternity → 14 weeks at 80% through EO
5.3% of AHV/IV/EO contributions are paid by the employee, while the total with the employer reaches 10.6%. It is the first step to read the average salary by profession in Switzerland in 2026 without confusing the gross with what remains in the paycheck in the canton of St. Gallen.
For statistics, the reference is FSO/BFS. The median salary is one of the figures indexed each year: the precise amounts must be checked against the correct year and the official source. An unverified value cannot become a 2026 figure attributed to a profession or the canton of St. Gallen.
### The tax perimeter The tax framework follows a separate logic. In Switzerland, there are three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax. FTA/ESTV manages IFD and VAT, cantonal administrations cantonal and municipal taxation. FSO/BFS produces statistics, does not set rates; FSIO/BSV concerns social security and does not set taxes.
### Payroll Entries The transition from gross to net requires isolating contributions. AHV/IV/EO is 5.3% for the employee and 10.6% overall with the employer. AD/CA is 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. UVG/LAA is indicated between 0.7% and 1.5% depending on the sector. BVG is calculated on the coordinated salary: 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54, 18% from 55 years old up to the reference age.
The minimum wage completes the reading of the labor market: there is no federal threshold, while some cantons have their own rules. Working conditions also matter: the maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 in other sectors; holidays are at least four weeks, five under the age of 20. Maternity lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave two weeks.
For a first simulation of the transition from gross to net, the calcolatore stipendio can be used. ### Three accounts not to be mixed A useful comparison for the canton of St. Gallen should put three levels on the same sheet: salary data, deductions and departures that are not withheld. The median salary is among the figures indexed each year; for 2026, only the value for the correct year should be used. A salary statistic does not describe the net or the cost of living on its own.
| Voice | Practical question | |---|---| | Salary | Which profession, industry and year are compared? | | BVG | Which age group and coordinated salary apply? | | KVG | Which canton or region, deductible and premium reduction? | | Taxes | Which three levels and which municipal multiplier? | | Cost of living | Which expenses are left out of the paycheck? |
The easiest place to make mistakes is the KVG. For residents, it is mandatory and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival, but it works with per capita premiums: it is not a tax and it is not a wage contribution. The premiums depend on the canton and region, while the premium reduction is cantonal. For adults, the deductibles indicated are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500.
For the same gross, the result may change if the relevant age group for the BVG, the canton or region of the KVG and the tax municipality change. In the canton of St. Gallen, the municipal multiplier must therefore be kept separate from the cantonal law: the municipality applies its own multiplier on the cantonal tax. Without an updated official rate, an invented percentage does not have to be entered. VAT also remains within the federal tax perimeter of the FTA/ESTV, not among the withholdings to be confused with AHV, ALV, UVG or BVG.
To complete the picture of expenses, place the costo della vita in Svizzera next to it and check the LAMal e cassa malati.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to check an offer for 2026
### Five-Step Procedure 1. Define the scope. Write down the profession, industry, canton of St. Gallen and year 2026. Look up the statistical data at FSO/BFS and check that any median salary refers to the correct year. Do not replace a missing figure with an estimate.
2. Start from gross. Separate AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVG. Record 5.3% payable by the employee for AHV/IV/EO, 10.6% overall with the employer, 1.1% ALV/AC up to the annual ceiling and 0.7–1.5% UVG/LAA depending on the sector. For BVG, use the coordinated salary and the expected age group.
3. Add the KVG. If you live in Switzerland, you must take out insurance within 3 months of arrival. The premium is per capita, not a tax or a wage contribution; check canton or region, adult deductible and possible cantonal reduction. The deductibles indicated are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 or 2500.
4. Reconstruct the tax system. Divide direct federal, cantonal and municipal tax. For IFD and VAT, the reference is FTA/ESTV; for cantonal and municipal taxes, the cantonal administrations. Consider the multiplier of the municipality, without assigning rates to FSO/BFS or FSIO/BSV.
5. Check the contract. Check the minimum wage: there is no federal threshold, but some cantons have their own. Then compare maximum hours, holidays, maternity, paternity and termination: 45 or 50 hours depending on the sector, at least 4 weeks of vacation, 14 weeks of maternity leave at 80%, 2 weeks of paternity leave; the termination is 1 month in the first year, 2 from the second to the ninth and 3 from the tenth.
To sort the busta paga svizzera entries and link them to the cost of living, use a simulation consistent with the year and canton. For the final net calculation, open the calcolatore stipendio.

### The salary figure and the correct perimeter
The median salary is among the figures indexed each year. For 2026, the verification must therefore start from the official figure referring to the correct year, without replacing an outdated figure with the relevant one. The comparison makes sense when it brings together homogeneous professions and sectors and separates the national level from the cantonal focus on Bern.
The FSO/BFS produces statistics, but does not set rates. For taxation, the FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT; the cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal components. The FSIO/BSV, on the other hand, concerns social security, including AHV/IV/BVG, and does not set taxes. The salary must then be read together with the contributions. AHV/IV/EO weighs 5.3% on the employee and 10.6% overall with the employer; AD/AC is at 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. The UVG/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. A comparison between Bern and the national framework only becomes practical when the salary figure is separated from the rules that accompany it. ### Four variables to put in the same tab
| Voice | Rule to check | |---|---| | Minimum wage | No federal level; some cantons have their own threshold | | Tax | Federal IFD, cantonal tax and municipal tax | | KVG/KVG | Compulsory insurance for residents; premiums by canton or region | | Lease | Maximum deposit of three months; escrow account in the name of the tenant |
The Swiss tax system operates on three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier to the cantonal tax. The tax result linked to a remuneration should therefore be read by separating the federal component from the local component, without assigning the FSO/BFS the task of setting rates.
The KVG is different from a wage deduction. For residents, it is a compulsory, private insurance with per capita premiums; premiums vary by canton and region, and premium reductions are a cantonal subsidy. For adults, the deductibles are CHF 300, 500, 1000, 1500, 2000 and 2500. This item is considered in costo della vita in Svizzera, not in addition to salary contributions.
The house also changes the practical reading of income. The CO Art. 253 et seq. establishes the same federal rules in each canton: the security deposit does not exceed three months' rent and goes to an escrow account in the name of the tenant. The landlord's notice of termination is only valid on the official cantonal form and the complaint must be submitted to the conciliation authority within 30 days.
Finally, the comparison between occupations must also record working time: the maximum limit is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 hours in other sectors. 2. Check the applicable minimum wage. There is no single threshold at federal level; some cantons have their own. The comparison must therefore distinguish the national framework from the rule of the canton in question.

4. Keep taxation separate. Direct federal tax and VAT are part of the FTA/ESTV; the cantonal and municipal parts are the responsibility of the cantonal administrations. The FSO/BFS provides statistics, while the FSIO/BSV concerns social security and not tax rates.
5. Add expenses that are not wage contributions. The KVG is mandatory for residents and must be taken out within three months of arrival. Premiums depend on the canton and region, premium reductions are cantonal and adult deductibles follow the options provided. Do not include this insurance in taxes or salary contributions.
The final sheet should report separately the salary data, working conditions and related exits. In addition to the maximum working hours of 45 or 50 hours, it records the minimum holidays, equal to four weeks or five under 20 years of age. item.description: In the canton of Graubünden, the course combines legal form, commercial register, minimum capital, registration fees and insurance obligations.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Legal form, register and minimum capital are the first issues. - The Swiss tax authorities operate on three levels. - FTA/ESTV follows IFD and VAT; the cantons the local levy. - AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG and BVG have an impact on wages.

### The perimeter of the start Opening a business in the canton of Graubünden requires keeping the corporate project and the cost of management separate. The choice of legal form, registration in the commercial register, minimum capital, registration fees and insurance obligations belong to the same path, but they are not the same item. An orderly estimate must therefore distinguish what is needed to start the business from what is used with taxation and wages.
The first reference is the tax system. In Switzerland, the levy has three levels: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies a multiplier on the cantonal tax. In Graubünden, this distinction prevents a single multiplier from being read as if it represented the entire tax account.
Administrative responsibilities must also be divided. The FTA/ESTV deals with direct federal tax and VAT. The cantonal administrations manage the cantonal and municipal components. The FSIO/BSV covers social security, including AHV/IV and BVG, but does not set taxes. The FSO/BFS produces statistics and does not set rates. For a new job, confusing these roles can lead to putting the correct entry in front of the wrong office.
The practical point is to separate the opening cost from the operating cost. The registration fees belong to the start-up; taxation, on the other hand, follows the three levels provided, while insurance obligations can be linked to salaries or, for the KVG, to residence. To prepare the dichiarazione delle imposte, it is advisable to keep the entries in the register, tax and insurance separate from the start. ## From the register to recurring costs
### When the business takes on The registration fee is a start-up item; the cost of labour, on the other hand, follows each salary. If the business in Graubünden has employees, the bill must be calculated on the contributions indicated from the source, without confusing them with taxes. The AHV/IV/EO is 5.3% borne by the employee and 10.6% overall by the employer. The ALV/HC is 1.1% up to the annual ceiling. The UVG/LAA varies from 0.7% to 1.5% depending on the sector. For BVG/BVG, the rates on the coordinated salary are 7% between 25 and 34 years old, 10% between 35 and 44, 15% between 45 and 54 and 18% from 55 years of age up to the reference age.

The table is used to distinguish between a payroll charge and a tax. In addition, the ALV/AC ceiling should not be converted into a fixed figure if it is not checked for the reference year. The indexed figures change every year; the same caution applies to the BVG coordination threshold and deduction, the average KVG premiums and the median salary.
The KVG/KVG follows another criterion. For those residing in Switzerland, it is mandatory and must be taken out within three months of arrival. It is a private insurance with per capita premiums, not a tax or a salary contribution. Premiums change by canton and region, while premium reduction is cantonal. In the family budget, therefore, the cost of living and the paycheck must be read on separate levels: the health premium is not calculated as a percentage of salary. If the business takes over, the working rules also apply. There is no federal minimum wage, although some cantons have their own. The maximum working time is 45 hours per week in industry, offices and sales, or 50 hours in other sectors. The minimum holidays are four weeks, five under the age of 20; maternity leave lasts 14 weeks at 80% through EO and paternity leave two weeks. ### Five Steps to Order Quote 1. Define the legal form. To build the estimate, associate the chosen form with the minimum capital provided for by the course and keep this item separate from the registration fees. 2. Isolate start-up costs. Record commercial register fees as a separate entry and do not merge them with future taxes or payroll contributions. The distinction makes it possible to understand which disbursements belong to the opening and which to the management. 3. Separate tax competences. For direct federal tax and VAT, the reference is the FTA/ESTV; for the cantonal and municipal part, the cantonal administrations are responsible. The municipal multiplier should be read as applied to the cantonal tax, within a three-tier system. 4. Prepare the work block. If there are salaries, set up the calculation with AHV/IV/EO, ALV/CA, UVG/LAA and BVP/BVG. Use the annual ceiling of the ALV/HC, the sector for the UVG/LAA and the salary coordinated with the age group for the BVG, without replacing these parameters with outdated amounts. 5. Check residence and staff rules. For residents, the KVG must be concluded within three months of arrival; premiums and reductions depend on the canton and region. If you are hiring, plan schedules, holidays, maternity, paternity and notice periods according to the indicated limits.
The check does not end with registration. The figures indexed each year include the 3rd pillar 3a ceiling, the BVG coordination threshold and deduction, the AD/AC ceiling, the average KVG premiums and the median salary. For this reason, a quote built with a fixed figure risks quickly becoming outdated: the parameters must be updated on the official source before using them.
### A readable file The clearest sequence is therefore the legal form and capital, register and start-up fees, taxation, salaries and insurance, then an annual review of the indexed values. item.title: Guy Parmelin announces his resignation from the Federal Council
item.description: The head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs will leave office on 31 December 2026. Excluding health reasons: 'I feel a certain tiredness'.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Parmelin to leave the Federal Council on 31 December - Health is not the reason for resignation - The Jans hypothesis opens up on the EAER - Duties, agriculture and housing await the successor
## Key Facts - Decision → resignation from the Federal Council - Deadline → 31 December - Place of announcement → Bern - Current position → Head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs - Stated reason → a certain tiredness - Hypothesis for EAER → Jans - Themes for the successor → US tariffs, agriculture and housing
### The conference in Bern On 2 October 2026, at 11 a.m., Guy Parmelin convened a press conference in Bern at short notice. The Federal Councillor, currently head of the Federal Department of Economic Affairs, announced his decision to resign from the Federal Council at the end of the year. He will cease his duties on 31 December.
The first clarification concerned health. In front of the media, Parmelin said that his condition had nothing to do with the choice. Back pain had repeatedly fueled speculation in the media about a possible resignation, but the president of the Confederation separated that issue from the political decision.
> "I feel a certain tiredness: the sacred fire is no longer as sacred as it was at the beginning."
Parmelin explained that he had thought long and hard during the summer break about what was best for the country. Progressively, he added, retiring at the end of the year seemed to him to be the most appropriate decision. He also said that he had taken enormous pleasure in leading the department and wanted to make room for new forces in times of great uncertainty.
The President of the Confederation reported that he had informed his colleagues that morning, during the weekly meeting of the executive. ## Key facts - Publication → 2 October 2026 - Location → Bern - Body → Federal Council - Mandate → postulate 24.3007 of CAPTE-S - Historical criterion → initial capacity of at least 10 kilowatts - Reference year → 1914 - Complementary statistics → installed capacity of at least 300 kilowatts - Document → 1.77 MB PDF
On 2 October 2026, at its meeting in Bern, the Federal Council took note of the report in fulfilment of postulate 24.3007 of the Environment, Spatial Planning and Energy Committee of the Council of States, referred to in the communiqué by the acronym CAPTE-S. The communiqué presents the act as the taking note of the report, published as a Federal Council document.
The report has a defined scope. It provides an overview of hydroelectric facilities with an initial capacity of at least 10 kilowatts that were in operation in the reference year 1914 and still exist today. The three elements must be read together: the initial-capacity threshold, operation in the specified year and the continued existence of the facility.
### What Bern publishes
The inventory concerns historic hydroelectric facilities in Switzerland. The communiqué presents it as a complement, not a replacement, to the statistics on Switzerland's hydroelectric facilities. The latter records operating facilities with an installed capacity of at least 300 kilowatts.
The distinction is essential for reading the document correctly. The historical inventory uses the initial capacity and the threshold of 10 kilowatts; the statistics referred to use the installed capacity and the threshold of 300 kilowatts. The time criterion is also different: for the inventory, the reference to 1914 and the existence indicated by the source matter, while the description of the statistics is limited to operating facilities.
The text released on 2 October does not state the number of facilities, their locations, the capacity of each one or any subsequent interventions. item.title: Parmelin resigns: the business community thanks him
item.description: The 66-year-old Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin announced his resignation today; Economiesuisse and the FSVO praise its agreements with India, Vietnam and renewal with China, as well as the Corporate Relief Act in force from 2024.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Guy Parmelin announced his resignation today. - Economiesuisse and the FSV praised his economic achievement. - Agreements mentioned: India, Vietnam and the start of renewal with China. - The Business Relief Act has been in force since 2024.
## Key Facts - Decision → resignation announced today - Age → 66 years - Department → EAER - Agreements → India, Vietnam and start of renewal China - Business Relief Act, in force → 2024 - Training → Professional Bachelor and Professional Master - Date → October 1, 2026 - President of the USC → Markus Ritter
Federal Councillor Guy Parmelin's decision to resign, announced today, has also provoked reactions from the business world. Monika Rühl, Director of Economiesuisse, expressed regret for the choice and paid tribute to the 66-year-old's merits in the business world.
> Parmelin has worked tirelessly for a strong Switzerland as a business location.
According to Rühl, numerous free trade agreements of great importance to the exporting Confederation have been negotiated under her leadership. The director thanked Parmelin for the good cooperation.
Economiesuisse considers the commitment of the successor of the People's Party leader at the head of the EAER to be decisive for a competitive Swiss business location. From an economic point of view, Rühl stressed, the department must remain in bourgeois hands.
### Trade, business and training
The FSVO also expressed its appreciation for the departing Federal Councillor. In its financial statements, the association described Parmelin's work in economic policy as exceptional, with particular reference to the free trade agreements with India and Vietnam. It also attributed to Parmelin the initiation of the renewal of the free trade agreement with China.
Among the internal policy measures, the FSVO cited the law on the relief of companies, which came into force in 2024. It then referred to the revision of the vocational education and training legislation and the enhancement of tertiary level professional education and training through the additional titles Professional Bachelor and Professional Master, which came into force on 1 October 2026.
For the FSVO, Parmelin was a valuable partner in social partnership and took employers' demands seriously. As President of the Confederation, the association adds, he represented Switzerland successfully and with dignity.
### The USC Assessment
Markus Ritter, president of the Swiss Farmers' Union, praised Parmelin's leadership and ability to maintain calm and overview. He recalled the extraordinary challenges of the mandate: the coronavirus crisis, the war in Ukraine, the unpredictability of American trade policy over the past two years, the fire in Crans-Montana and the landslide in Blatten (VS). The Vaud politician, he added, was a crisis manager: with the Americans, he contributed to the search for solutions thanks to his French-speaking charm and convincing arguments, also choosing qualified personnel for his entourage. ## The point of operation for those who work
The clearest practical consequence concerns the succession at the helm of the EAER. In its reported reactions, Economiesuisse points to the competitiveness of Switzerland as a business location as a criterion for the successor. The source does not give the name of the future manager or describe an immediate measure for companies, employees or families: the step to be taken is therefore political and institutional, not a new individual procedure.
### Foreign trade as an indicator
The free trade agreements referred to by Economiesuisse and the FSVO define the foreign dossiers associated with Parmelin's budget. India and Vietnam are mentioned directly; for China, the source speaks of the start of the renewal, not of an agreement that has already been renewed. For exporting companies, this signals a political priority. However, it does not allow for the indication of sectors, costs, revenues, hires or deadlines: these data do not appear in the text.
Internally, the Business Relief Act and Vocational Education and Training have a distinct relevance. The former is referred to as a measure that came into force in 2024. The Professional Bachelor's and Professional Master's degrees, on the other hand, are presented as additional qualifications to tertiary level vocational education and training, which have been in force since 1 October 2026. The source does not specify requirements, costs, procedure or effects on employment contracts.
### Positions and decisions
The demand to keep the EAER in bourgeois hands is a position of Economiesuisse, not the name of a successor. Similarly, the FSVO's assessment of the social partnership describes the relationship it had with Parmelin and its focus on employers' demands; it does not announce new rules.
Markus Ritter's assessment adds the perspective of agriculture and crisis management: calm, oversight and the ability to deal with the Americans. Here, too, the source offers a judgment on the mandate, not a specific measure for farmers or the labor market.

To use this news without overlapping different plans, it is worth proceeding by verification. The announcement of the resignation, the assessments of Economiesuisse, FSO and USC and the dossiers mentioned in Parmelin's financial statements do not have the same weight: the first concerns the announced decision, the second are judgments, the last are economic policy and education issues.

The law is indicated as coming into force in 2024; for Professional Bachelor and Professional Master, the source indicates October 1, 2026. The announcement remains dated only as today. 3. Those who follow agriculture can read the USC's judgment as an assessment of Parmelin's leadership, not as a new decision for the sector. item.description: Premiums in Ticino +3.7% in 2027 compared to the Swiss average of 5%. The average premium reaches 519.90 francs, +56% in a decade.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief
- In 2027, Ticino's premiums will increase by 3.7%. - The Swiss average premium rate will rise by 5%. - The average Ticino premium will reach 519.90 francs per month. - In a decade, the Ticino premium has grown by about 56%.
## Key Facts
- Author → Luca Frasa, Movimento giovani leghisti - Year → 2027 - Increase in Ticino → 3.7% - Swiss average → 5% - Average Ticino premium → CHF 519.90 per month - Growth in the last decade → about 56% - Compared to Zug → around 11% - Proposal → uniform premiums at national level
In 2027, Ticino will see health insurance premiums increase by 3.7%, compared to 5% of the Swiss average. The Council of State speaks of an encouraging sign and the first effects of the work done. Luca Frasa, of the Young League Movement, however, urges not to read yet another price increase as a victory.
> "Let's take note of it. But let's not turn yet another increase into a victory."
### The figure beyond 2027
The average Ticino premium will rise to 519.90 francs per month, still the highest in Switzerland. The percentage expected for 2027 comes after years of price increases that, according to the author, have hit the canton harder than others. The message therefore does not only concern next year's change, but the path that preceded it.
In the last decade, the premium in Ticino has grown by about 56%. In other cantons the increase has been much lower; in Zug, for example, it is around 11%. The comparison shows the distance accumulated over time, without canceling the fact that the Ticino annual figure is lower than the expected Swiss average.
For Ticino families, writes Frasa, these are not abstract percentages. It is money that every month is added to rents, energy, shopping, mobility and a cost of living that continues to put pressure on purchasing power.
### The funding proposal
The issue is presented as structural. The KVG is federal and compulsory benefits are governed by the same law throughout Switzerland; however, financing through premiums produces enormous differences between one canton and another. In recent days, Frasa reports that he has coordinated with Alessandro Mazzoleni, deputy in the Grand Council of the Lega dei Ticinese.
Mazzoleni then presented a cantonal initiative to ask Bern for a modification of the KVG: uniform premiums at national level for the same age, deductible and insurance model, together with a national distribution of the costs of compulsory care. To accompany the public data with a verification of the insurance issue, confronto cassa malati e LAMal is available. ### How to Really Interpret the Increase
The first practical step is to distinguish the pace of the increase from its starting level. An increase below the national average is still an increase: it does not mean that the premium is decreasing or that the burden on the household budget will automatically be reduced. The news says that Ticino will grow less than the average in 2027; it also says that it starts from an already very high average level.
The second step is to separate a single year from the trajectory. A budget built only around the next adjustment risks overlooking the effect of previous years. The comparison with Zugo is precisely meant to show this trajectory: in Ticino, growth over the last decade was much more pronounced. The figure therefore raises a question about how spending is financed, not just about its immediate change.
| Reading perspective | What it means for a family | |---|---| | Annual increase | Measures the expected increase for 2027 | | Average premium | Provides a monthly reference for Ticino | | Ten-year evolution | Shows the cumulative effect of increases | | Comparison between cantons | Highlights regional differences | | Financing | Takes the debate beyond the percentage alone |
### From Premium to Monthly Spending
The source places the premium alongside rent, energy, groceries and transportation. Therefore, the practical interpretation does not consist in memorizing a percentage, but in checking how much room remains each month after these expenses. The cost of living is not presented as a separate item: it is the overall pressure on purchasing power.
The political issue concerns the structure. If mandatory benefits are regulated by the same LAMal throughout Switzerland, the place where a person lives still affects the bill through the premium mechanism. The proposal brought to Bern changes the perspective: not only how to slow increases, but how to finance a mandatory federal social insurance scheme.
The idea of uniform premiums for people with the same age, deductible and insurance model, with a national distribution of the costs of mandatory care, opens up a focused debate. The reader can separate two questions: how much the premium affects their budget today and what criterion should distribute the costs among the cantons. 1. Set the horizon. Write 2027 at the top of the card and note the average Ticino premium indicated in the source as a parameter of comparison with your monthly invoice. 2. Separate expenses. Keep health insurance, rent, energy, spending and mobility on different lines so that you can see which costs are affecting your budget together. 3. Compare the levels. Record the expected increase for Ticino, the Swiss average and the evolution of the last decade without confusing the annual figure with the accumulated one. 4. Divide the two plans. On the one hand, place the expenditure that weighs today; on the other hand, note the discussion on the modification of the KVG and the financing criteria.
This method helps not to use the national comparison as an automatic response to the situation of each family. The average premium is a reference for Ticino, while the concrete pressure arises from the set of monthly expenditures. The sheet also allows you to check whether the increase is assessed alone or together with the rest of the cost of living.
In order to follow the political proposal, the points to be kept separate are those indicated in the cantonal initiative: uniform premiums at national level, age parity, deductible and insurance model, as well as the national distribution of the costs of compulsory care. In this way, the debate remains anchored in readable criteria and not just in the percentage of the year.

item.title: ETH study: poor and rich pay the same taxes
item.description: Research by ETH Zurich reveals that almost everyone pays 45% of their income. Only the richest 1% pay less due to health premiums and VAT.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - The overall system amounts to approximately 45% of gross income. - Only the richest 1% pays a lower share. - Health insurance premiums and VAT weigh more heavily on lower incomes. - The ETH method includes taxes, transfers and government benefits.
## Key facts - Study → Swiss Federal Institute of Technology Zurich (ETH) - Researcher → Isabel Martinez, ETH KOF Institute - Overall share → approximately 45% of gross income - Bracket paying the least → richest 1% - Burdens mentioned → health insurance premiums and VAT - Method → overall national income, taxes, transfers and government benefits - Wealth → grows faster than incomes - Investments → stocks, including in the third pillar
Approximately 45% is the share of gross income that, according to the ETH study, is paid by all social groups. Only the richest 1% pays less. The research was presented by Isabel Martinez, a researcher at ETH Zurich's KOF Institute, in an interview published by Beobachter in its current issue. The news was reported by Keystone-ATS.
The point of the research is the gap between the progressivity envisaged for some taxes and the outcome of overall taxation. Income tax and, in part, wealth tax are structured progressively: those who earn more pay more. But, according to Martinez, health insurance premiums and VAT are left out of this initial view, independent of income and a heavier burden on lower-income groups. In the middle-income bracket, by contrast, employment income and the social contributions levied on it carry more weight. The issue of cassa malati premiums is therefore central to the explanation.
> «All social groups pay approximately 45% of their gross income: only the richest 1% pays less».
### Why the picture is broader When asked whether, despite the Federal Constitution, taxation is not based on ability to pay, the economist replies that this conclusion can be reached by looking at taxes and contributions together. The study did not consider only taxable income and wealth. It used total national income from the national accounts and included taxes, transfers and government benefits, calculating who receives what share before and after these levies and interventions.
The calculation includes supplementary benefits, pensions and health-insurance subsidies, but also undistributed corporate profits and tax-advantaged dividends intended for majority shareholders. For Martinez, including all these incomes makes the picture more precise and more unequal.
Finally, the study links growing inequality to wealth. In Switzerland, wealth grows faster than incomes, but the advantage goes to those who own wealth: those who do not own a home do not automatically benefit from rising property prices. Returns on wealth can then fuel further income inequality.
Martinez also urges caution regarding stocks. Investing savings, for example in the third pillar, has become easier, but understanding the market and choosing the right product is more difficult than comparing mortgages. This difficulty, she concludes, can create uncertainty and discourage. ## How to read the levy in the balance sheet
The ETH figure is not equivalent to the rate indicated on an individual return. It measures the share of national income that remains after the set of taxes, contributions and benefits, or that which is redistributed through state interventions. For a resident, the practical check must keep the levels of Swiss tax separate: direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax. Each canton has its own law and multiplier; the municipality applies its multiplier to the cantonal tax. The comparison between two budgets can therefore also change depending on the tax location.
### Entries not to be confused The table helps to reconstruct the transition from gross income to the overall burden:
| Voice | How it enters the reading | What to check | |---|---|---| | Income and wealth taxes | They are structured progressively | Portion paid in relation to income | | VAT | It is independent of income and is mainly levied on low incomes | Weight on expenditure | | KVG/KVG | Premiums are per capita, not a tax or a wage contribution | Cantonal premium and reduction | | Social contributions | Are levied on income from employment in the middle range | Deductions from wages | | State benefits | Includes pensions, supplementary benefits and health insurance benefits | Amounts received |
This distinction avoids confusing the progressivity of the tax with the cost of living. KVG/KVG premiums vary by canton and region, and the premium reduction is cantonal; for residents, insurance is compulsory. The source points to premiums as one of the reasons why the overall burden weighs relatively more heavily on low incomes, alongside VAT and social security contributions.
For those who work on a salary, the transition from gross to net also includes pension contributions such as AHV/AHV and BVP/BVG, while pension benefits enter the considered transfer side. For those who do not own real estate, the comparison changes again: rising property prices do not produce an automatic profit, while assets generate returns.
### The useful comparison The practical question is not only what tax is paid, but what items remain after deductions and what benefits are received. A balance sheet that records taxes, VAT, premiums, contributions and transfers offers a reading closer to the ETH method. To learn more about the territorial effect on costo della vita in Svizzera, it is advisable to keep the tax and health items separate.
## Useful planning tools To estimate your pension strategy, use the pension planner and the pillar 3 simulator. ## How to do a personal verification
The source does not propose a simulation for the individual taxpayer, but its method suggests a concrete sequence. The goal is not to look for a single rate: it is necessary to reconstruct gross income, separate withdrawals and benefits and distinguish assets from their returns. It is a broader reading than one based only on income or taxable assets.
### Four operational steps 1. Start with gross. Write down your earned income and any property income. Separate the pre-tax portion from the after-tax portion. If there are retained earnings or subsidized dividends, the research will look at them in the big picture.
2. Separate the tax authorities. Put direct federal tax, cantonal tax and municipal tax in different columns. The canton applies its own law and multiplier; the municipality uses the multiplier on the cantonal one. This avoids comparisons based on a single item.
3. Isolate health and consumption. Record the KVG/KVG premiums separately from VAT. For those residing in Switzerland, the KVG is mandatory and must be taken out within 3 months of arrival; the premiums are per person and depend on the canton and region. Also check the cantonal premium reduction, without treating it as a complete cancellation of the disparity described by the source.
4. Look at your assets. If you don't own real estate, don't automatically attribute rising house prices to you. If you evaluate stocks or the role of retirement provision, you can delve into AVS/LPP/rendita; don't turn the article into investment advice. Martinez warns that understanding the market and choosing the right product is more difficult than comparing mortgages. The third pillar is cited by the source as a possible area for investing savings, but caution remains necessary.
The final audit must put gross, taxes, VAT, premiums, contributions, benefits and assets side by side. This is how the comparison sticks to the method described and does not exchange a single deduction for the entire cost of living. ### The transfer of ownership Micasa changes hands again: a group of Swiss investors has taken over 100% of the shares of the furniture retailer. The company announced the transaction on Friday to the AWP agency, confirming what was anticipated by Inside Paradeplatz. The names of the investors have not been disclosed.
However, the operational leadership remains in the hands of Philipp Agustoni, CEO, and Manuel Landolt, COO. According to the company, the new ownership will bring additional capital, entrepreneurial experience and expertise in the areas of logistics, digitalization and technology. The share change is therefore accompanied by a strengthening indicated by the company on specific operating areas, without changing the two main managers of management.
### The four locations involved The plan is to close four of the 30 Micasa branches. The Crissier site will permanently lower its shutters by the end of 2026. Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs will follow by the end of January 2027. The reason given by the company is the current economic situation and the changed market conditions.
Alternative solutions are being examined for the employees involved. The communication does not associate a different outcome for each location for the staff: the only element indicated is that the alternatives are still being examined. For customers, the calendar therefore distinguishes an initial deadline for Crissier and a subsequent one for the other three branches.
This is the second change of ownership in less than two years. In February 2025, Migros sold Micasa through a management buy-out to a consortium led by Agustoni and Landolt, with the participation of the German and Austrian investor families Brandstetter-Finger and Wiest. Since 1 September 2025, Micasa AG has been operating independently.
The company is active in the mid-price segment and compares itself on the market with Ikea and XXXLutz, among others. The new operation therefore changes the ownership of Micasa, while communication maintains the operational direction and declared positioning. ### A more concentrated network
The most readable operational data for those who use the points of sale is the concentration of the network: the communication concerns four out of 30 branches, not the entire brand. The difference between the deadlines counts. Crissier has the end of 2026 as its deadline; Langendorf, Brügg and Buchs follow by the end of January 2027. Those who have to deal with one of these locations must therefore start from the location, not from a single date valid for the whole of Micasa.
The transition must be read on two levels. On the one hand, there is the continuity of management: Agustoni and Landolt remain responsible for operations. On the other hand, the owner changes, with 100% of the shares acquired by a group of Swiss investors. The company links this new phase to additional capital, entrepreneurial experience and expertise in logistics, digitization and technology. These are the concrete elements indicated to accompany the management, while the communication does not present an additional timetable for the network.

## In brief - Over a thousand Aeropers members sign an open letter - Swiss's new CEA is still under negotiation - Asked for more free time, less load and market pay - Swiss calls for costs, competitiveness and tight deadlines
## Key Facts - What → open letter to the management of Swiss - Who → more than 1000 members of the Aeropers association - Topic → new collective bargaining agreement - Demands → better leisure planning, less workload and market-adjusted pay - Status → negotiations that have been ongoing for some time
ZURICH - More than 1000 members of the Aeropers association have signed an open letter addressed to the management of Swiss. The position comes during the dispute over a new collective employment agreement, the CEA for cockpit staff.
Aeropers recalls in a statement today that negotiations have been underway for some time. At the center are three demands: better planning of free time, less workload and pay appropriate to the market. The letter thus makes the position of the pilots visible while the negotiations remain open.
### The Company's Location
According to Thomas Steffen, spokesman for Aeropers quoted in the note, the signatures show the cohesion of the staff and at the same time indicate the urgency of intervention. The association's message therefore links the number of adhesions to the need to achieve results on working conditions.
Swiss's management responded through an internal communication from CEO Jens Fehlinger to the pilots. The manager showed understanding for their requests and indicated that many of the topics raised are also societal issues.
Swiss says that it has been working with Aeropers on new working models for some time and is negotiating intensively on the topics mentioned. However, the company also refers to economic pressure and cost developments.
According to Fehlinger, the new CEA will have to take into account both the needs of pilots and Swiss's long-term competitiveness. His communication also contains a call to accelerate progress. "Time is running out," concludes the CEO.
The available content therefore describes an open dispute, with increasing pressure from the association and a corporate response that acknowledges the issues raised but also recalls costs and competitiveness. An outcome of the negotiations is not announced: the new CEC remains the focus of the confrontation between Swiss and Aeropers. ## What the negotiation brings into play
For those who work in Switzerland, the dispute compares three dimensions of the employment relationship: the organization of time, the workload of the activity and the remuneration. It is therefore not just a question of economic demand. Aeropers also brings to the table the way in which leisure time is planned and the overall pressure incurred by pilots.
The call for better leisure planning draws attention to the predictability of work organisation. The source does not describe a concrete model, but clearly indicates that time management outside the work is one of the points to be changed according to the pilots. The lower workload concerns the intensity of the activity and is presented as a separate request.
Remuneration adapted to the market opens the third level of discussion. The text does not indicate amounts, increases or a new salary scale. For this reason, the request cannot be transformed into an increase already decided: it remains one of the subjects negotiated in the new CEA.
### The balance point for Swiss
The company considers the needs of pilots, but also recalls economic pressure, cost trends and long-term competitiveness. The company's position therefore introduces a double criterion: improving working models and maintaining the company's competitive sustainability. The source does not disclose what solution can reconcile these two objectives.
For the reader, the practical distinction is between the request, the position of the management and the outcome of the negotiations. The letter signals a strong support of the staff, while Swiss's communication shows openness on the issues but does not announce an agreement. The story concerns Swiss and the cockpit staff; it does not allow requests to be automatically extended to other companies or professions.
Anyone who observes the opportunities in the sector can consult the annunci di lavoros, without treating the dispute as a change already applied to employment conditions. The comparison with the aziende che assumonos must also remain separate from the still negotiated content of Swiss's CEA.

### Four useful steps
1. Separate the documents. The open letter represents the position of the Aeropers members who signed it; the internal communication expresses the point of view of Swiss's management. They are two different messages within the same dispute.
2. Write down the three requests without adding details: better time off planning, less workload, and pay appropriate to the market. The source does not provide amounts, new operating rules, or a definitive timetable.

## In brief - On 2 October 2026, the Federal Council selected eight projects - Planned funding: CHF 135 million - Sectors: energy, public transport and water resources - Proposed budget: CHF 3 million to CHF 30 million
## Key Facts - Decision → 2 October 2026 - Location → Bern - Programme → National Programme for Ukraine 2025–2028 - Projects approved → eight - Planned funding → CHF 135 million - Proposal budget → CHF 3–30 million - Own funds → at least 10% of the costs - Competitive selection procedure →
On 2 October 2026, the Federal Council approved eight projects by Swiss companies in Bern to support reconstruction in Ukraine. The decision is part of the national programme for Ukraine and provides for funding of CHF 135 million for initiatives in the areas of energy, public transport and water.
The measure is part of a program that already finances projects by Swiss companies to strengthen the resilience of Ukraine, described in the press release as a war-torn country. The logic indicated is operational: to make Swiss products and technical know-how available to meet urgent needs.
### A selection for Swiss companies
The projects were selected through a competitive procedure. Swiss companies with a branch in Ukraine were invited to submit proposals with a budget of between CHF 3 million and CHF 30 million. The initiatives had to respond to an urgent need for support from Ukraine and be implemented by local companies.
The evaluation followed criteria established in advance by both parties: relevance, impact on development, technical feasibility, risk, resource efficiency and Swissness. For the selected projects, the companies will also have to cover at least 10 percent of the costs from their own resources.
The final selection took place in collaboration with the Ukrainian government, based on the country's needs. The press release refers to an attached table with the list of the eight projects, without indicating their names in the text. The practical significance for the Swiss economy focuses on the relationship between the federal decision, Swiss companies and activities carried out on site. The scope indicated by the press release is precise: the procedure concerned Swiss companies with a branch in Ukraine, committed to submitting projects for urgent needs.
The before and after are just as clear. The national programme for Ukraine already financed initiatives by Swiss companies; the decision of 2 October 2026 approved eight further projects. The funding thus links Swiss products and technical know-how to interventions in the energy, public transport and water sectors.

item.title: Switzerland initiates consultation on the third ECAG Protocol
item.description: The Federal Council opened the consultation on the third CEAG protocol on 2 October 2026, which will close on 19 January 2027; Switzerland signed the text in Malta on 19 September 2025.
item.content:encoded:
## In brief - Federal Council launches consultation on 2 October 2026 - The procedure ends on January 19, 2027 - Switzerland signs the Protocol on 19 September 2025
## Key Facts - Subject: → Third Additional Protocol to the CEAG - Consultation → launched on 2 October 2026 - Deadline → 19 January 2027 - Swiss signature → Malta, 19 September 2025 - Ratification → Parliament
## The passage decided by the Federal Council
During its meeting on 2 October 2026, the Federal Council initiated the consultation procedure on the Third Additional Protocol to the European Convention on Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters. The procedure will be completed on 19 January 2027. Switzerland has already signed the protocol: it was signed in Malta on 19 September 2025 at the informal conference of ministers of justice.
The European Convention on Mutual Assistance in Criminal Matters, or CEAG, is an agreement of the Council of Europe. Switzerland is a contracting party to it. Its structure links criminal cooperation to respect for individual rights: fair trial, proportionality of state interference and protection against arbitrariness.
### What does the CEAG govern?
The CEAG obliges the Contracting States to assist each other in cross-border criminal prosecution. Examples include the taking of evidence through the hearing of witnesses, experts or accused persons. The Convention also lays down the procedure and conditions for the submission and execution of letters rogatory.
The new protocol stems from the Council of Europe's objective of making the fight against cross-border crime more efficient, while maintaining compatibility with the rights of the accused. The Committee of Ministers of the Council of Europe adopted it before Switzerland's signature. In the communiqué, the Third Protocol is presented as a step in the modernisation and harmonisation of cross-border criminal prosecution in Europe.
Among the innovations mentioned is the possibility of transmitting letters rogatory electronically, taking into account technological developments in modern media. Switzerland contributed to the drafting of the text, in particular on the provisions relating to the cross-border use of technical recording devices, such as GPS trackers, and the surveillance of telecommunications traffic. Parliament will have the final say on ratification.
The timetable distinguishes between three institutional steps: the signature of the text by Switzerland, the start of the consultation by the Federal Council and the subsequent decision by Parliament on ratification. The consultation is therefore the step indicated by the Federal Council before the parliamentary decision. ## What changes on the operational level
In order to understand the scope of the dossier, it is necessary to separate what the CEAG already provides for from the additions to the Third Protocol. The Convention requires the Contracting States to assist each other in cross-border criminal prosecution and regulates the submission and execution of letters rogatory. The Protocol, on the other hand, focuses on the electronic transmission of requests and the adaptation of cooperation to modern means of communication.
### Three areas to observe
The first concerns evidence. The basic text provides for the hearing of witnesses, experts and defendants; the reader can therefore distinguish the content of the request from the way in which it is transmitted. The second concerns technology: the communiqué indicates new electronic possibilities for letters rogatory. The third includes provisions on the cross-border use of technical recording devices, including GPS trackers, and on the surveillance of telecommunications traffic.
For those who live or work in Switzerland, the concrete interest is procedural. In a criminal case involving several countries, the points to be followed are the collection of evidence, the rogatory and the guarantees relating to the accused. In fact, the source links the efficiency of the fight against cross-border crime to fair trial, proportionality of state interference and protection from arbitrariness. The dossier therefore concerns judicial cooperation.
The Swiss signature and consultation do not coincide with ratification. The path indicated goes through the procedure initiated by the Federal Council and arrives at the decision of Parliament. The press release does not describe any effects on other areas of national life. Those who are looking for tax information must keep this dossier separate from the dichiarazione delle imposte.
## Useful tools to protect your net income To reduce FX leakage, compare CHF-EUR exchange options and banks for cross-border workers. ## How to follow the Swiss route
To read the dossier without confusing the different moments, it is worth constructing a documentary sequence. The first reference is Switzerland's signature, which took place on 19 September 2025 in Malta. The second is the Federal Council meeting on 2 October 2026, which opened the consultation. The third is the deadline of 19 January 2027. Only after this step, according to the communiqué, will Parliament decide on ratification.
### Documents to be compared
The page of the press release lists the explanatory report for the start of the consultation procedure, the draft federal decree approving the Third Protocol, the text of the Third Protocol and the English version. The most useful reading sequence is to start with the report, move on to the draft and then check the technical provisions in the Protocol.
In the reading, four operational questions can be isolated. Which passages of the CEAG concern the taking of evidence? Where does the Protocol provide for new possibilities for the electronic transmission of letters rogatory? Which provisions concern technical recording devices and the surveillance of telecommunications traffic? How is the reference to the rights of the accused, fair trial, proportionality and protection against arbitrariness maintained? These are all axes already present in the communiqué and help to distinguish the rules of cooperation from technological tools.
The last check concerns the status of the process: signature, consultation and ratification are different steps. Parliament still has to decide on ratification, while the consultation has a precise closing date. ## In brief - Federal Council approves dispatch - The ceiling remains at CHF 10 billion - The proposed extension runs until April 2033 - IMF transfer worth around CHF 90 million
## Key Facts - Decision → 2 October 2026 - Legal basis → the Monetary Assistance Act of 19 March 2004 - Deadline of the decree → April 2028 - Proposed extension → April 2033 - Maximum amount → CHF 10 billion - Swiss share for the IMF fund → around CHF 90 million
### The approved passage in Bern On 2 October 2026, the Federal Council approved the dispatch on the continuation of international monetary assistance in Bern. The text submitted to parliament proposes to extend the Monetary Assistance Decree until April 2033. The extension is therefore a proposal by the Federal Council submitted to Parliament, not a decision already approved by Parliament.
The framework set out in the communiqué is based on the Monetary Assistance Act of 19 March 2004 and the corresponding Monetary Assistance Decree. The latter allows the Confederation to provide international monetary assistance up to a maximum total amount of CHF 10 billion until April 2028. In the dispatch, the Federal Council proposes to extend the validity of the decree until April 2033 while keeping the ceiling unchanged.
The stated aim is to enable Switzerland to continue to participate rapidly in measures to stabilise the global financial system if necessary. The communiqué therefore presents a longer time horizon for the same maximum amount, without announcing an increase in the commitment credit.
### The IMF chapter At the same meeting, the Federal Council reiterated Switzerland's support for the IMF trust fund for the poorest countries. Switzerland's share of IMF resources allocated to this fund, amounting to around CHF 90 million, can be used to reduce the interest on IMF loans to poorer countries.
The resources generated by the IMF will be transferred within the IMF itself, provided that a majority of its members approve the procedure. The source also specifies that the transfer will not have financial repercussions for the Confederation. ### Relevance for Switzerland For those who live or work in Switzerland, the decision is primarily institutional. The communiqué concerns the Confederation's ability to provide international monetary aid and to participate rapidly in measures for the stability of the global financial system. However, it does not describe a procedure aimed at individual residents, employees or companies.
Practical reading requires separating three passages, which have different functions in the text:
| Step | Status described in the source | |---|---| | Monetary Assistance Decree | Allows international aid until April 2028, up to a total of CHF 10 billion | | Dispatch from the Federal Council | Proposes to parliament an extension until April 2033, with the same amount | | IMF Trust Fund | Switzerland's share of around CHF 90 million can reduce interest if a majority of members approve the procedure |
The comparison between these phases avoids confusing a proposal with a parliamentary decision that has already been concluded. If Parliament approves the proposal, the horizon indicated by the decree may reach April 2033 while maintaining the same ceiling. However, the source does not present the outcome of this step.
The transfer linked to the IMF is also subject to a specific condition: a majority of members must approve the procedure. The text therefore does not present the transfer as an operation unrelated to further decisions. Instead, it specifies that the resources will be transferred within the IMF and that there will be no financial repercussions for the Confederation.
For the reader, the distinction is also useful on a personal level: the ceiling of 10 billion francs concerns international monetary assistance from the Confederation and is not presented as a sum to be paid or received individually. 1. From the date of the decision, 2 October 2026, and from the institution that adopted it: the Federal Council. 2. Refer to the Dispatch on the granting of a commitment credit for the continuation of international monetary assistance in the years 2028–2033, published as a document dated 2 October 2026. 3.
